NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
MECHANISM CLASS: Settle-Phase Duty Modulation
The question is answered by retuning the SBR's settle-and-decant timing procedure to extend the low-shear settling window and shift the decant initiation to a later time point, directly mitigating poor-sludge-settling-decant. Standard practice uses a fixed, default settle hold duration (typically 15–20 min) and immediate decant initiation; this mitigation departs by extending the settle hold duration to 30–45 min and delaying decant initiation, exploiting the extended quiescent period to allow floc consolidation and bulk density increase prior to supernatant removal. The adjacent-technique clearance is that extending settle time is a recognized SBR operation lever, but the departure is the specific pairing of extended quiescence with delayed decant initiation within the fixed reactor volume and without any aeration or flow modification during the settle phase, ensuring zero shear. The mechanism attacks the failure’s driving physics by increasing the time available for gravitational sedimentation to overcome the hindered settling regime and floc fragmentation, thereby raising the settled sludge blanket density and lowering the turbidity of the decanted supernatant.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Supernatant turbidity $T_{dec}$ is inversely proportional to the settled sludge blanket density $\rho_{blanket}$ and the settling time $t_{settle}$, governed by the Stokes’ law terminal velocity $v_t = \frac{g d^2 (\rho_p - \rho_l)}{18 \mu}$ and the hindered settling correction $\phi = \frac{v}{v_t}(1 - \phi_0)^{[n]}$.
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = floc fragmentation rate and hindered settling exponent $\phi_0$; the mechanism moves settling time $t_{settle}$ up by 15–25 min (a 50–100% increase over standard 15–20 min) and moves decant initiation time up by the same delta; this reduces the decant turbidity integral $\int_0^{t_{dec}} T(t) dt$ by allowing the sludge blanket to consolidate into a denser phase before supernatant withdrawal, lowering $T_{dec}$ by 20–40% relative to the fixed-timing baseline.
INPUT-AVAILABILITY: The remedy requires only the existing SBR timer/controller (stated infrastructure) and the visual or level-based decant gate already used in standard practice; no new sensors or analysis channels are required, and the timing is open-loop, so all inputs are derivable from the constraint’s permitted procedure axis.
COST-PRICING: The operational loss is a throughput reduction of 15–25 min per SBR cycle (approx. 10–15% of total cycle time), which is a zero-energy and zero-material loss; the trade nets positive because decant quality improvement reduces downstream filtration load and avoids effluent exceedance penalties, and the loss is explicitly scheduled within the non-aerated settle phase where no energy is consumed.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. **Retune SBR Control Logic Setpoint**: Modify the "Settle Hold" timer value in the existing SBR controller from its standard 15–20 min setting to 30–45 min, and correspondingly extend the "Decant Initiation" timer by the same delta. Tag (c): parameter/duty change to existing control equipment, no new hardware.
2. **Procedure Change – Zero-Shear Settle Verification**: Operate the existing settle phase with all aeration and mixing stopped (already standard practice for SBR settle), confirming zero flow rate and zero pressure differential across the reactor for the extended duration; no physical installation or modification is made to the reactor, aeration, or decant lines. Tag (c): procedural change on stated equipment at its rated settings.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Installation: No new hardware, tools, or parts; burden is identical to the standard practice’s own controller reprogramming (zero physical install).
Commissioning: A single 24-hour run at the new setpoint to verify decant quality; burden is a standard SBR cycle verification, same class as routine SBR commissioning.
Operation: The extended settle time is a pure time extension with zero energy or material cost; operational loss is 15–25 min/cycle (approx. 10–15% throughput), explicitly priced and netted against downstream quality gains.
Maintenance: No new maintenance tasks; the control timer is part of the existing SBC and requires no additional service.
Conclusion: Same-or-lower burden class; the only delta is a schedule extension, which carries zero hardware burden and a fully priced operational loss.
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run the SBR at the standard 15–20 min settle for 5 cycles as baseline; measure decant supernatant turbidity ($T_{base}$). Then run 5 cycles at the extended 30–45 min settle and delayed decant; measure decant turbidity ($T_{new}$). Instruments: Existing SBC turbidity meter or visual/photometer (stated in standard practice); no new instrumentation. Pass/fail: $T_{new} \leq 0.7 T_{base}$ (a $\geq$20% turbidity reduction) AND no increase in cycle time beyond the priced 15–25 min/cycle. Duration: 10 cycles (5 baseline + 5 intervention), approx. 2 days. Kill criterion: If $T_{new} > 0.8 T_{base}$ after 5 intervention cycles, the mechanism fails; revert to standard timing and document the negative result.
